study type: Nationwide register-based nested case-control study and matched cohort study
cohort: The study included 1,803,309 singleton pregnancies of 1,041,419 women recorded in the Swedish Medical Birth Register during 2001 to 2018.
finding: The study found a bidirectional association, where premenstrual disorders were associated with a higher risk of subsequent perinatal depression (OR 4.76) and women with perinatal depression were at higher risk of subsequent premenstrual disorders (HR 1.81).
followup_time: 7.40 years (mean follow-up for the matched cohort study investigating PND to PMD risk)
